text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for dedicated pool `eu-west-1-pool-37` (streaming stalls increasing). Auto-pager: paging @oncall-sre — 07:42 UTC
jamie.sre: ACK'ing. I'm on it. noticed p95 creeping too. anyone grabbing dashboards? :eyes:
lucas.runtime: grabbing metrics now — load graph shows sudden queue depth spike at 07:40, sustained for ~3m. snapshot: p95=420ms, p99=2.6s, streaming_stall_rate=6.8% (baseline ~0.4%).
priyanka.ops: autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts for pool-37 starting 07:39. Handshake failures to provisioned instances: "handshake_timeout" and failed warmup hooks. Suspect warmup latency causing requests to pile up.
jamie.sre: can you paste the autoscaler errors?
priyanka.ops: log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T07:39:12Z] scaler: request_scale_up delta=+2 target=6 -> 8
[2026-03-15T07:39:13Z] scaler: launch vm id=i-0abc... status=initializing
[2026-03-15T07:39:45Z] warmup: kvcache-warmup failed for vm i-0abc... reason=timeout
[2026-03-15T07:40:05Z] scaler: launch vm id=i-0def... status=initializing
[2026-03-15T07:40:40Z] warmup: handshake_timeout for vm i-0def...
[2026-03-15T07:41:00Z] queue: pool-37 depth=142 processing=6 throughput_drop=32%
```
lucas.runtime: that matches what I'm seeing on runtime traces — new nodes are not reaching ready state before traffic is routed. continuous-batching holds requests and streaming connections stall until KV warmup completes.
rachel.support: FYI we have an open ticket from ACME (cust-id: cust-9982) reporting long responses and partial streams. they've pasted request IDs: rq_77a2, rq_77a7. We should surface expected ETA.
jamie.sre: immediate mitigation suggestions: (1) temporarily divert new requests for pool-37 to compatible fallback pool (eu-west-1-pool-21) with lower load; (2) pause autoscaler to stop thrashing; (3) manually add 2 warm nodes with forced warmup and hold traffic until ready. Which one can we do fastest?
tom.platform: diverting routing policy is fastest. I can flip route-weight for model variant `rw-v1-compat` -> 80% to pool-21 in 90s. Command: 
```bash
# internal routing API
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://internal.redwood/api/route/update \
  -d '{"pool":"eu-west-1-pool-37","fallback":"eu-west-1-pool-21","weight":0.2}'
```
priyanka.ops: manual scale will take ~3–5m to provision and warm. If we route now, queue depth will drain quickly. I can also set a force-warmup job: `opsctl warmup --pool pool-37 --mode forced` once the nodes are up.
nina.custops: I'm drafting a short customer update for ACME: "We detected elevated latency in your dedicated pool and are routing your traffic to a lower-latency pool while we stabilize. Expect improvements within minutes. We'll follow up when resolved." Want to confirm before sending 
jamie.sre: good — send the note once routing flip is done and include the two request IDs so support can correlate.
lucas.runtime: one more datapoint: streaming worker logs show KV cache coldpath misses spike from 2% -> 48% during the window which explains stall behavior. If we keep routing, we avoid cold starting additional nodes while we stabilize.
priyanka.ops: doing two things now: (A) applying manual route change to shift new traffic to pool-21, (B) pausing autoscaler for pool-37 to manual mode to prevent further scale attempts. I'll post commands and results.
priyanka.ops: (command run) `POST /internal/route/update ...` -> 202 Accepted. (command run) `PATCH /internal/autoscaler/pools/pool-37 {"mode":"manual"}` -> 200 OK.
jamie.sre: monitoring queue depth and p99 after route flip. please call the bridge for quicker coordination: meet at +1 minute?
nina.custops: bridge call started: https://meet.redwood/bridge/incident-2401234567 (call on)
(rachel.support adds :thumbsup: reaction)
jamie.sre: p99 dropped to 1.1s after partial routing, p95 now ~350ms. queue depth draining (142 -> 28). streaming_stall_rate -> 1.5%. progress but not fully recovered.
lucas.runtime: recommend still to bring nodes up with forced warmup to rebuild capacity and reduce cross-pool routing. I'll start warming once you allow scale.
priyanka.ops: I'll bring pool-37 to +2 nodes but keep them in standby (no traffic) until warmup completes. warming job kicked off. warmup logs show progress: index fetch, kvrestore, model init.
jamie.sre: good. next steps: (1) keep autoscaler paused for 15m, (2) once warm nodes report healthy, re-enable routing back to pool-37 gradually (10% increments), (3) re-enable autoscaler only after two full warm cycles.
tom.platform: I'll prepare an automated rollback in case p99 jumps during ramp: route rollback playbook `playbooks/route-backoff` ready.
rachel.support: ACME update sent: "We've routed your requests to a lower-latency pool; our engineering team is actively stabilizing your dedicated capacity. We'll follow up when we return traffic." they replied: "Thanks, saw improvement."
jamie.sre: handoff — I'm going to step off the bridge in 15m. lucas, can you take watch for next 30m and escalate to SRE lead if p99 > 1.5s for >3m?
lucas.runtime: taking handoff. I'll keep bridge open and post metrics every 5m.
jamie.sre: misc notes for postmortem: timeline, autoscaler handshake/timeouts, coldpath KV misses, routing decisions, customer impact (ACME), mitigation commands and why autoscaler pause was necessary. assign to priyanka for infra root cause, lucas for runtime traces, and myself for incident writeup.
priyanka.ops: noted and assigned. I'll collect autoscaler state, cloud provider logs, and warmup traces.
nina.custops: closing loop with ACME later with a short summary and the postmortem link once ready.
jamie.sre: thanks everyone — will post a short incident summary in #incidents when we have final metrics. Handing over. :white_check_mark:
